entry.title: JavaScript Private Elements Trump Compile-Time Illusion
entry.summary: After spending years building systems that demand true encapsulation and security boundaries, I’ve witnessed countless debates about privacy mechanisms in JavaScript. The introduction of JavaScript private elements (MDN) marked a fundamental shift in how we think about encapsulation in the language. While TypeScript’s private modifiers have served us well as training wheels, it’s time to acknowledge that JavaScript’s native private elements represent the superior approach for building robust, secure applications at scale. TypeScript’s private modifiers operate purely at compile-time. They’re suggestions, not enforcements. Once your TypeScript compiles to JavaScript, those private modifiers vanish like morning mist. entry.title: GhostLayer - AI Text Humanization - My first app launching
entry.summary: I've officially purchased a domain to launch my app: http://ghostlayer.io.vn/ This app helps humanize text so it won't be flagged as AI-generated. In other words, it transforms AI-generated content into natural, human-like writing while preserving meaning and intent. Beyond those who frequently use AI to write content, there are people who write their own content but still get incorrectly flagged by AI detection tools. This happens because they've learned writing styles from standardized tests like IELTS and TOEFL—the same sources these AI systems were trained on—leading to false positives. My app helps prevent these situations. When you search for it on Google right now, this app hasn't been indexed yet and won't show up in results since it typically takes several weeks or even months to get indexed and appear in search results, so just bookmark it first. Hopefully, one day many people will use this app. Even if it won't go viral, it'll serve as valuable experience for my other apps. I'll post a demo video later showing how it works.

entry.title: Building Offline Apps with Next.js and Serwist
entry.summary: LocallyTools has been live for a while now. Although the product uses browser capabilities to process data locally, users kept questioning its credibility—"Are you sure my files won't be uploaded?" "How can I prove that data won't leak?"
